subject: alienFlora
pitch:
Category: Plant.
Subject: bioluminescent alien plant.
Style: Avatar.

spec.name: Lumivine Spire-Bloom
spec.description: A Pandora-style bioluminescent alien plant: a curved, ridged stem crowned with eight huge arching leaves veined in glowing cyan, a magenta-and-white flower core, hanging glow-bulb tendrils, and a ring of luminous ground flora at its feet.
spec.layout: A single hero plant, centred on x=0, standing on y=0. From the side the silhouette is a tall S-curved stem (leaning very slightly toward +Z at the top) that flares into buttress roots at the base. The stem ends in a crown at about y=2.55 holding eight broad, drooping-then-upturned leaf fronds fanned out radially (reaching about 1.35 m from the axis, with the two front fronds pointing toward +Z). Their upper surfaces are deep teal and their undersides violet. The fronds are the largest shapes. A glowing flower bulb with a ring of white and magenta petals and gold stamens rises from the middle of the fronds, topping out at y=3.3. From a ring around the crown just under the fronds, long thin tendrils hang down 0.8-1.3 m, each ending in a glowing bulb. Around the base lie a low mossy mound, glowing mushroom disks, spiral fan plants and sprouts, all inside a 2.6 m footprint. Avatar/Pandora look: dark indigo-teal bodies (flat colours, lit by place: lighter teal moss on top faces, violet shadow undersides), and every glowing piece is a small part in its own bright flat colour wrapped in glow(). Glow is used with discipline: cyan veins and rims on the leaves, magenta tips and bulbs, mint and violet spots on the stem and ground. The model is built from blocky, faceted primitives with low segment counts (6-8 sides), and the character comes from repeated motifs: glowing vein lines, dotted spots, and paired spirals.

parts.builds: Foundation. A low faceted soil/rock mound (flattened lathe or squashed 8-sided spheres in soilDark and rockBlue) about 1.9 m across and 0.35 m high, topped with mossTeal and mossLight patches on the upward faces. Six to seven thick buttress roots (tapered sweeps, trunkDark shading to trunkMid) flare out from the stem base at mound level, curve down into the soil and reach about 0.9 m from the axis. Each root carries a thin glowing vein line (veinCyan or glowViolet) and a few small glowing nodes (glowMint). Some pale moss tufts and small pebbles sit on the mound. Colour by place: light moss on top, soilDark at the edges, violet shadow at the root undersides.
parts.attaches: The root tops converge on stemBase, where the stem tube starts. The mound top is at moundTop; the ground flora part sits around and on the mound's outer edge.

parts.builds: The main stem: one smooth-skinned sweep or loft through stemBase, stemMid, stemUpper and crownBase, with the joints base, stem1, stem2, stem3 and crown as its bone list. Radius is about 0.26 at the bottom, narrowing to 0.17 at the waist and flaring to 0.24 under the crown. The section is a faceted 7-8-sided ngon coloured by trunkDark with countershaded sectors (trunkMid on the sides, trunkLight along the up-facing back, shadowViolet underneath). Details: 8-10 raised ring ridges (barkRidge) around the stem, small spiralling rows of glowing spots (glowMint and veinCyan, about 3 cm) winding up the stem, 3-4 short side spurs/nubs with glowing tips (glowMagenta), a glowing vein line running up the front (veinCyan, thin sweep on sweep.line or sweep.at), and a collar of small trunkLight scales where the stem meets the crown. The crown collar is a short flared lathe at crownBase that the fronds and bloom rise from.
parts.attaches: Starts at stemBase (inside the root cluster) and ends at crownBase, where the collar sits. The fronds' stalks root in the collar at frondRing and the tendrils' tops attach under it at tendrilRing.

parts.builds: Eight huge leaf fronds fanned radially around frondRing, the dominant silhouette. Each has a thick tapered stalk (sweep, trunkMid) rising out 0.25 m and then a broad leaf blade (extrude with smoothing, leaf outline with a pointed tip, about 0.55 m wide by 1.1 m long, thin) that arches up and out and droops toward the tip. Fronds rotate in 45° steps; two point forward (+Z) and two back, with alternating lengths (1.1 and 0.9 m) and elevation (some lifted +25°, some drooping -15°) so the crown is not uniform. Upper faces are leafMid with a leafTeal edge strip; a leafDeep strip runs on the midrib; undersides use shadowViolet (a second slightly larger offset blade or sectors). Glowing detail on each blade: a central midrib (veinCyan sweep) with 4-5 pairs of angled side veins (thin extruded or swept lines, veinCyan fading to glowMint farther out), a glowMagenta rim blob or spike at the tip with tipPink highlight, and 5-6 small dots (glowBlue) near the edges. Use glow() on the veins, tips and dots only; leaf bodies are not glowing.
parts.attaches: Stalks root at frondRing on the stem collar and ride the joint crown. They leave the middle free: the bloom rises from bloomCenter inside the ring of stalks, and the tendrils hang from tendrilRing below the blades.

parts.builds: The flower and the hanging tendrils. (1) The central bloom at bloomCenter: a small squat stalk (trunkLight), a glowing bulb core (8-sided sphere, glowMagenta, about 0.16 m radius) wrapped by two rings of petals (extrudes with pointed outlines, inner ring petalWhite, outer ring tipPink fading to glowViolet), 6 petals each, opening upward to y=3.3 at the tallest. In the middle stands a cluster of 7-9 thin stamens (swept lines, stamenGold, each ending in a small glowing glowMint bead) and a pistil spike (veinCyan). Four floating spore motes (small octahedron/sphere parts, glowMint and glowViolet) hover 0.1-0.4 m above the petals. (2) Tendrils: 12-14 thin, gently curved sweeps hang from a ring of radius 0.4 at tendrilRing (just under the fronds), down 0.8-1.3 m with varied lengths and slight swing outward, coloured by gradient (trunkMid at the top to glowViolet at the bottom). Each tendril has a glowing bulb at its tip (alternating glowMagenta, glowBlue, glowMint, 3-5 cm) and 2-3 small beads strung along it. A few hang forward and low as shorter tassels. Keep all tendrils at least 0.32 m from the stem axis so they do not cut into it.
parts.attaches: The bloom stalk rises from bloomCenter above the stem collar and sits between the frond stalks. The tendril tops attach on tendrilRing under the crown collar and hang down alongside the stem.

parts.builds: Luminous understory growing around and on the outer edge of the mound, inside a 2.6 m footprint but outside radius 0.5 around the stem. (1) Five to six mushroom/disk plants: thin stalks (trunkMid) with flat 8-sided cap discs (leafMid or shadowViolet) from 0.08 to 0.25 m wide, each with a glowing underside ring (glowBlue or glowViolet) and glowing rim dots (veinCyan). (2) Three spiral fan plants (Helicoradian-style): short stem sweeps that carry a spiral ring of thin leaflets or fans (6-8 thin extruded blades around a ring, leafTeal with glowMagenta tips), up to 0.55 m tall; at least one in each front quadrant. (3) 12-16 sprout shoots: tiny curled tendril sweeps (spiral paths) with a glowMint or glowMagenta bead at the tip, 0.1-0.4 m tall, plus tufts of 4-5 thin blades of leafTeal/mossLight. (4) 6-8 glowing seed pods lying on the ground (squashed 6-sided spheres, glowViolet and glowMint, 4-8 cm) and a handful of small rocks (rockBlue). Spread everything evenly, with the front (+Z) in the same density as the back, and keep every piece grounded.
parts.attaches: Rests on the floor at the mound's edge and lightly on its outer slope (mound top at moundTop is at most 0.4 m high); keeps clear of the buttress roots near the stem.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out a spec for a bioluminescent alien plant in the Pandora style, with a central tree-like form, large fronds, hanging tendrils, glowing spiral plants, and ground pods. I'm setting the bounding size at 2.6 wide, 3.2 tall, and 2.6 deep, centred, and wondering whether the plant should be a static model or something with simple objects.

I'm now weighing whether the plant needs a few simple joints for sway or should stay fully static, and I'm leaning toward a small chain of base and stem joints with a bloom, since the parts can attach to them. I'm also sketching the overall look: a tall curved stem with a crown of large glowing fronds, bell-like and spiral.

I'm laying out the parts of the plant now: a root base with buttress roots, a mossy mound, and glowing pods around the ground, all within a box about 2.6 wide and 0.5 tall. Next comes the stem, a sweeping trunk with ridges, glowing nodes, and spiral stripes, ending at a crown point near the top. Last, I'm planning eight large crown fronds arching outward from that point, with glowing veins, each around 1.2 long.

I'm now setting the bounding box for the crown fronds and tendrils. The crown's bounds run roughly from -1.3 to 1.3 across, with the fronds arching up and down. I'm adding a central bloom with petals, a glowing stamen, and drifting spore motes, plus hanging tendrils with glow bulbs at a radius of about 0.35 from the crown, reaching down toward y≈1.2. I'm checking that the tendril volume doesn't clash with the stem or the frond undersides, and budgeting 200 for this part.

I'm finishing the ground flora for the plant: three spiral fan-like plants, glowing mushroom disks, and luminous grass blades, all inside a box about 2.6 by 0.9 by 2.6 with a flat floor, budgeted at 160. I'm also checking that the parts add up to around 890 and that the overall size of 2.8 by 3.3 by 2.8 still fits the fronds and the bloom.

I'm placing the joints now: a base at the root, then three stem joints rising up the trunk, with the crown joint sitting at the top of the stem.

I'm wiring the stem to follow the chain of joints from the base up to the crown, sweeping it through their positions since they're already created. I'm also settling on a palette of around twenty colours, with deep indigo and teal darks and cyan, magenta and violet for the glow.

I'm settling the colour palette now: about twenty tones, with deep indigo and teal darks and cyan, mint, magenta and violet for the glow, and I'm noting that the glowing parts should use a shared glow helper.

I'm going to write buildFrondCrown, weighing whether to type the Ctx parameter loosely as any or to define a local alias, since it may already be provided globally.

Still working out the frond geometry: eight fronds spaced 45° apart around the origin, each stalk running outward and rising, with the blade built as two extruded segments so it can arch up and then droop toward the tip.

Still working on the blade: I'm splitting it into two extruded segments, with the thickness axis set so the blade stays roughly vertical and the tip comes out pointed.

Still working on the frond blade: I'm setting the second segment to droop about 55° below the first, and I'll offset an underside blade slightly larger and lower, using the blade's normal to place it.

Still working on the frond blade: I'm sweeping the midrib along the blade's centerline and a thin edge rod along each side, with a flat deeper strip just below it.

Still writing the side veins: a few pairs running from the midrib out toward each edge, with the inner ones in cyan and the outer ones in mint.

Still writing the crown code: I'm adding a magenta spike at the tip with a small pink marker, then blue glowing dots placed near the edges, and starting the stalk as a curved sweep.

Still writing the stalk and blade placement: I'm pinning the blade's base about 0.3 out from the axis and 0.18 above the ring, and capping the first segment's lift so the top stays under the box.

Still working on the frond layout: I'm angling the eight fronds at 22.5° offsets, alternating lengths and elevations so two sit forward and two back, and trimming the first segment so the blade stays under the box.

Still writing the frond blade geometry: I'm defining the width profile so the leaf narrows to a sharp tip, sampling the lower edge up to the point and the upper edge back down.

Still writing the outline: I'm sampling the lower edge up to the tip and the upper edge back down, with the tip point handled so it doesn't duplicate.

Still writing the frond blade: I'm placing each segment's frame from its direction and side vectors, and adding an underside blade slightly offset along the normal.

Still writing the frond geometry: I'm adding a rounded edge strip along each side of both blade segments, with the sweep following the outline across the bend.

Still writing the midrib: a polyline of points sampled along the blade's centerline, with a thin vein sitting slightly above the blade surface.

Still writing the stalk: a sweep through three points from the base outward and up to where the blade starts, with rounded caps.

Still writing the code: I'm settling the stalk's start point and the frond's reference frame, then setting up the Vector3 alias and the types.
